nodes.text: 1. Form 3 of Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers-Disclosure scheme will be enabled shortly

2. Due dates for filing of Income Tax Returns and Audit Reports for AY 2026-27 are extended in the cases of persons mentioned at Sl.No.2 in the Table below Explanation2 to Sub-section (1) of Section 139 of Income Tax Act 1961 vide Circular No.07/2026 dated 28th September,2026.
3. Form 1 under the “Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers Disclosure Scheme” is now available for filing.
4. ITR-1, ITR-2, ITR-3, ITR-4, ITR-5, ITR-6 and ITR-7 for AY 2026-27 are available for filing through both online and offline utilities.
5. Filing of TDS/TCS Correction Statements pertaining to Tax Year 2026-27 has been enabled.

6. Demand Management Facilitation Centre (DFC), has been set up to guide Taxpayers on issues/grievances regarding their outstanding demands. DFC may be contacted through the e-mail id: taxdemand@cpc.incometax.gov.in or on the toll-free number - 1800 309 0131 or chargeable no. 0821-6671200.
7. Excel utilities for filing Updated return for ITR-1 to 7 for AY 2022-23 as per Finance Act, 2026 are available for filing !

A  is a word, name, logo, symbol, design, or combination that distinguishes the goods or services of one business from those of others. Registration provides statutory protection and helps the owner establish exclusive rights over the mark for the registered goods or services.
Provides statutory rights against unauthorized use of the registered mark.
Gives the owner exclusive rights to use the mark for the registered goods or services, subject to applicable law.
Helps customers identify and distinguish a business and its products or services.
A registered trademark is an intangible asset that can be licensed, assigned, or commercially exploited.
Helps prevent unauthorized use of identical or deceptively similar marks in relevant circumstances.
Trademark registration is governed by the  and administered by the Trade Marks Registry under the .
Controller General of Patents, Designs & Trade Marks (CGPDTM)
A search is conducted to identify existing identical or similar marks and assess potential conflicts before filing.
The application can be filed online through the  portal. It generally includes:
Applicable trademark class under the Nice Classification
Power of attorney, where filed through an agent or attorney
The Registrar examines the application under the Trade Marks Act. If objections are raised, an  is issued and the applicant may submit a response.
If the application is accepted, it is published in the  to allow third parties to oppose the registration. The statutory opposition period is  from publication.
If no opposition is filed, or any opposition is resolved in the applicant's favour, the trademark is registered and a registration certificate is issued.
A registered trademark is generally valid for  from the date of application and can be renewed indefinitely for further 10-year periods.
Trademark logo or wordmark, where applicable
Other supporting documents depending on the applicant and application
